correctness.rationale: Integral companion A of t^(2d)+k has det k and A^(2d)=-kI, distinct nonreal eigenvalues with common modulus r=k^(1/(2d)); conjugate eigenspaces yield an A-invariant complex structure and a Hermitian scalar-product homothety. Quotient by Z^(2d) yields the holomorphic k-sheet cover. Roots raised to n give gcd(n,2d) repetitions, proving the exact determinant count. Volume-change identity forces all expanding complex manifolds degrees >=2. The universal proof is analytic and not inferred from finite tests.

value.rationale: Degree is a fundamental global invariant of holomorphic expanding coverings. In a fixed positive complex dimension, naive coordinatewise multiplication produces degrees that are high powers, obscuring whether degree two or every integer can occur. The theorem gives a complete, sharp degree spectrum and realizes it even among globally Hermitian-homothetic maps, a severe geometric restriction, with explicit periodic data for each realization. This is not merely a numerical slice or renaming of an existing bound.
